The answer is **B**: the act of State doctrine means courts will not rule on the validity of a foreign State's public acts done within its own territory, so assessing an alleged State wrong is left to the executive. It is a rule of judicial abstention, not blanket immunity (A), and it does not treat courts as well placed to judge such acts (C). D is the closest distractor because it wrongly frames the doctrine as a grant of immunity.

CONFIDENCE: 90
